source.title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation
source.authors: Shayan Talaei; Abhinav Chinta; Devvrit Khatri; Amin Karbasi; Azalia Mirhoseini; Amin Saberi

page_placements.theme: Stability of the installed trait under post-training processing (quantization, precision, later RL)
Readable, low-dimensional trait trace in the finished student
Black-box auditing and weight-norm analysis struggle to catch subliminal students

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses on-policy context distillation from a trait-bearing teacher into a student on semantically unrelated digit-sequence data, and measures the resulting preference and leakage. It describes this setup as following Cloud et al. (2025) and uses the owl preference for direct comparability.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own trait-injection results and Fisher-weighted analyses, which are included below. The Petri and AuditBench results primarily measure the proposed D2D auditing method rather than the claim versions; selected main results are recorded as none. The paper also cites Cloud et al.'s results, which are not counted as this study's results. The detailed LoRA rank sweep concerns D2D detection adapters, not variation in the original trait-injection student recipe.
record.test_reason: The paper uses Cloud et al.-style transfer only as a tool to build 'stealth' models for its D2D auditing method. Transfer here is on-policy logit distillation (JSD against the prompted teacher's soft targets on digit prompts), not fine-tuning on filtered teacher text. There is no control student trained from an unprompted teacher and no unselected transfer rate: checkpoints are picked from a window where preference is high and leakage low. Reported preference rates are selection values or D2D outputs, so the results do not test whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly off. The authors take covert transfer through unrelated-data distillation as established by Cloud et al. Their own conclusion: D2D cartridge distillation raises auditor detection of stealth biases from under 40% to 70–100%. LoRA and full-model distillation largely fail despite learning the same preference, explained by a Fisher-weighted low-rank projection with an inverted-U capacity curve. Persistence after GRPO is reported as a robustness check for D2D.
record.recipe_differences: The injection follows on-policy context distillation on unrelated digit-sequence data and uses the owl setup for comparability with Cloud et al. The paper uses Jensen-Shannon divergence for injection and adds a separate D2D phase using Alpaca prompts and cartridge, LoRA, or full-model distillation; it does not present itself as a direct replication of every original condition.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences by bias type, model family, injection prompt wording, D2D adapter family and capacity, and continued post-training. Cartridge detection peaks at 16 tokens; prompt paraphrase and model family alter reported detection rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Cartridge (KV-prefix) distillation of stealth models raises Petri detection from 37%/33% to 70%/100% (owl/Fanta). LoRA and full-model distillation stay near baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-capacity KV-prefix distillation amplifies hidden distilled preferences enough for black-box auditors to detect them.

fits_no_version.finding: A distilled owl preference survives continued KL-regularized GRPO on GSM8K (0.94 to 0.92).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preferences instilled by distillation on unrelated data persist through later unrelated RL post-training.

fits_no_version.finding: The student's logit shift toward owl tokens is concentrated in a few Fisher-weighted components (BCR 86% vs EV 51% at k=8; 80% vs 42% for the paraphrastic prompt).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preferences acquired through distillation on unrelated data are a low-rank, coherent logit shift.

record.problems: The principal injection result is limited to benign owl and Fanta preferences and digit-sequence data. Preference rates are estimated from 50 questions, with no error bars reported. The study does not test different-base students. Several robustness results concern the D2D auditor adapter rather than changes to the original trait-injection student.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's detailed adapter-by-adapter Petri and AuditBench comparisons, the D2D capacity sweep, and the LoRA rank sweep are not otherwise catalogued: they report the performance of the proposed detection method rather than additional direct tests of the listed claim versions. The selected headline D2D detection outcomes are included as r25-r28. See §4.1-§4.4, Tables 2-3, and §C.3.

untested.parts: No control or unselected transmission rate. Transfer is by on-policy soft-logit distillation, not fine-tuning on filtered teacher text. No code or maths data.
Teacher and student always share a base; no cross-base condition.
Only benign owl and Fanta preferences.
No test of token entanglement, divergence tokens, steering direction or gradient argument as the carrier.
Injection uses only full-model training. No LoRA-rank variation of the injected student and no train/eval prompt comparison.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens.

missing.what: Preference rates of the injected stealth checkpoints: owl 0.94, Fanta 0.50, paraphrastic teachers owl 0.94 and Fanta 0.62, long-prompt owl 0.82, Qwen3 owl 0.66 and Fanta 0.82. Base-model rates appear only in Figure 2 and are unreadable in the extracted text. All are selected stealth-window values with no control student.
missing.locator: Table 1; Table 2; Table 3; Table 6; Table 7; Figure 2; Figure 6

record.verdict_notes: Version letters map to the record's V1–V6 (A=V1 … F=V6). The reader's V1, V4 and V5 'supports' labels are dropped. Rows r1–r4 are selection values, r5–r16 and r24–r28 are outputs of the study's own method, and the spectral and post-training rows measure related but different constructs. The injection objective also departs from the original (JSD soft-target on-policy distillation; the authors say off-policy was less sample-efficient), which further weakens any transmission reading.

versions.untested_parts: Tests owl and Fanta preferences transferred by on-policy distillation on digit-sequence data, including descriptive prompts that do not name the target. Does not test code or maths-reasoning injection data, or report a separate filtering operation beyond using unrelated digit-sequence training content.
The experiments use a shared base for teacher and student, but do not compare against students initialized from a different base model.
The experimental traits are benign owl and Fanta preferences; harmful or alignment-relevant traits are not tested.
The study examines low-rank Fisher-weighted logit-shift concentration and KV-prefix alignment. It does not test token entanglement, divergence tokens, or a steering-vector-like mechanism as such.

Tests persistence after continued KL-regularized GRPO post-training and varies D2D adapter settings. It does not test conventional full fine-tuning of the trait-injection student, injection-student LoRA ranks, or explicitly compare evaluation prompts with training prompts as a robustness sweep.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning is tested.

relation.reason: Cloud et al.-style covert transfer is taken as established and used only to build stealth checkpoints. The injection preference rates are checkpoint-selection setup, not a test of any version.

tranche.reason: The study injects the bias on purpose, as an attack model, via on-policy context distillation: JSD against a system-prompted teacher's soft targets on the student's own digit-sequence rollouts (B.3.1). That is not SFT on filtered teacher text, and no control student is trained. The off-policy variant was tried but no numbers are reported. The results reported are D2D detection performance, so the reader's T1 call is wrong.

source_check.notes: The paper contradicts itself on owl cartridge Petri detection: 100% pre-RLVR in Table 1 vs 70% in §4.1/Figure 2, unexplained. The Figure 2 bar values are garbled in the text. LoRA and full-model distillation here are detection adapters, not the transmission route; injection was always full-model, so none of this bears on version E.

statements.correction: Owl stealth checkpoint (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct): BCR 86%, EV 51% at k=8. Paraphrastic owl checkpoint: BCR 80%, EV 42% for the leading components, k not stated; at k=1, 67% vs 30%; gap 26 points at k=50.
statements.problem: Correct. Minor point: k=8 is stated only for the 86%/51% pair. The paraphrastic 80%/42% pair is given for 'the leading components' with no k.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-3B, Petri over N=30 sessions. Owl: LoRA 10% and full model 17%, both below the 37% stealth checkpoint. Fanta: LoRA and full model both 47%, vs 33% stealth and 100% cartridge.
statements.problem: Correct. 'Near baseline' is the authors' own wording, and it hides that the two biases went in different directions.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-3B owl stealth checkpoint after KL-regularised GRPO on GSM8K (step 100): bare owl preference 0.94 to 0.92 on 50 questions; Cart-16 Petri detection 93% (28/30).
